key_insight: Pretrained large language models extracted more useful signal from veterans’ clinical notes than bag-of-words methods for suicide risk prediction, especially when combined with structured EHR data.
clinical_relevance: This suggests unstructured clinical notes can add value to existing Veterans Health Administration risk stratification workflows such as REACH-VET.
method: Compared pretrained LLM text representations with classical bag-of-words features.
Used clinical notes from 27,241 U.S. veterans in the Veterans Health Administration.
Evaluated predictions across REACH-VET risk tiers and look-back windows of <30, <90, and <270 days.
evidence_signal: LLM-based representations outperformed bag-of-words in 7 of 9 tier-window settings, with text-only AUROC up to 0.644 and 0.748 when structured variables were added.
watch_item: Performance was modest and drawn from one health system, so external validation and careful deployment testing are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Comparative Evaluation of Pretrained Large Language Models for Suicide Risk Prediction from Clinical Notes in U.S. Veterans
